Box-I: COP30 Agenda and Pakistan’s Strategic Role

COP30 adopted the Belém Political Package, anchored in the Global Mutirão decision, with several outcomes 
of direct relevance to Pakistan. These included the launch of a Global Implementation Accelerator to support 
implementation of  Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs); a 
strong emphasis on climate finance, including a call to triple adaptation finance by 2035, establishment of a

two-year work programme on finance under Article 9.1, and enhanced ex-ante finance reporting (Article 9.5) 
to improve predictability and transparency and operationalization of the Loss and Damage Fund under the 
Barbados Implementation Modalities with an initial allocation of US $ 250 million, based on grant financing 
and simplified access. Progress was also achieved on the Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) through adoption

of 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators across key sectors, designed to remain voluntary and country-driven, 
reflecting Pakistan’s position on flexibility. Additional outcomes included establishment of a Just Transition 
Mechanism emphasizing nationally determined pathways and support for developing countries in 
operationalization of the Technology Implementation Programme (TIP) to accelerate technology transfer and 
innovation.
